records.why: The lesson title and several texts say a histogram or polygon shows WHERE the long gaps are or where pedestrians are at risk. A histogram of gap lengths has gap length on the horizontal axis, not distance along the road, so it shows the spread of gap sizes, not their location. Location comes from the ordered list of gaps (which the class already has). Leaving it would teach a real statistical misreading. Checked by re-deriving positions: G1-G8 sum to 1,550 m, G9-G14 span 1,550 m to 6,800 m, and 4,000 m falls inside G11 (3,250 m to 4,350 m). The lesson title is left unchanged because teachers chose it; it is covered by this note.
records.old: Do not re-teach mean or median calculation (done in Lessons 3 and 5).
records.new: Do not re-teach mean or median calculation (done in Lessons 3 and 5). Make one distinction explicit: a histogram shows HOW MANY gaps are short or long, not WHERE along the road they are. The positions (G9-G14, the school gate at 4,000 m) come from the ordered gap list G1-G20 and the pedestrian counts. If a learner points at a bar and says 'this part of the road', ask: 'The bar tells us how many gaps are that long. Which list tells us where they are?'
records.reference: OpenStax Introductory Statistics, Chapter 2.2 Histograms, Frequency Polygons and Time Series Graphs
records.group_headline: Histograms and polygons show how gap lengths are spread, not where the gaps lie on the road; the text now says location comes from the ordered gap list

records.why: The sub-strand had no language support for English learners. The Kiswahili terms are my suggestion and are not verified; the teacher must confirm the words used in their school and add terms for median, mode and class if wanted.
records.old: if asked, say 'We will test this in Lesson 3'.
records.new: if asked, say 'We will test this in Lesson 3'. Language support: write each key word on the board with an example and, where it helps, a Kiswahili term beside it (for example takwimu for statistics, wastani for average, jedwali la masafa for frequency table). Let learners talk in Kiswahili or their home language first, then say it in English. Teachers should confirm the terms they use.

records.why: Graph drawing is the most demanding task for learners with special needs; adds an alternative way to take part.

records.new: Provide extra support cards for learners needing scaffolding (for example pre-labelled axes). records.why: Teachers had no expected answer for the analogy and its limits were not stated. Mean recomputed: 500 / 5 = 100; median is the middle value of 20, 20, 30, 30, 400 = 30.
records.old: Pose the vegetable-price analogy and ask: 'Which number would you tell a new neighbour is the normal price?'
records.new: Pose the vegetable-price analogy and ask: 'Which number would you tell a new neighbour is the normal price?' Expected answers: KSh 30 (the median, and one of the two commonest prices) is the normal price; the mean, KSh 100 ((20 + 20 + 30 + 30 + 400) / 5), is higher than what four of the five households pay because KSh 400 pulls it up. Limit of the analogy: five households is a tiny sample with one extreme value, while the road has 20 gaps with six long ones.

records.why: Model answer; recomputed 5/9 x 200 = 111.1, so 311.1 m, matching Lesson 5.

(e) n = 20, so n/2 = 10. Cumulative frequencies: 5, 14, 14, 16, 17, 20. The 10th value lies in the class 200 to <400 (L = 200, cumulative frequency before it = 5, f = 9, w = 200). Median = 200 + ((10 - 5) / 9) x 200 = 311 m (311.1 to the nearest metre). This is an estimate; the true median is 250 m.

records.why: The CBE rubric has four levels (Exceeds, Meets, Approaches, Below Expectations) but the contract allows only three level fields, so Below Expectations cannot be represented. Suggestion: teachers add a fourth column by hand when printing, or the partner extends the contract.

KICD allots 16 lessons to Sub-Strand 3.1 Statistics I; this sequence has 8 lessons, now 600 minutes (15 lessons of 40 minutes). Not changed: the lesson count is fixed by the brief. Teachers may wish to check whether 600 minutes is enough for their timetable. KICD content (all five bullets) and all six outcomes are taught and assessed; the unit adds a Road Safety PCI that is not in KICD and is labelled as a suggested link.
records.reference: KICD Grade 10 curriculum design, Mathematics, Strand 3.0 Statistics and Probability, Sub-Strand 3.1 Statistics I

records.why: Round 2, journal item math_3_1-030 (teacher: 'Use 16 lessons but the last lesson can be used as a lesson for summative assessment'; KICD allots 16 lessons to Sub-Strand 3.1). The apply tool cannot insert or renumber lessons, so no lesson was added and no durations were trimmed (trimming 80 to 40 would contradict the teachers' 16-lesson request). Proposed split, every period 40 minutes: L1 -> 1+2, L2 -> 3+4, L3 -> 5+6, L4 stays 7, L5 -> 8+9, L6 -> 10+11, L7 -> 12+13, L8 -> 14+15 (the 8 existing lessons already say 2 x 40-minute periods, so the existing Pacing minute plans give the split points), and a new Lesson 16 for summative assessment (the Final Explanation, 40 minutes). That is 15 teaching lessons + 1 assessment = 16 lessons, 640 minutes total (totalDuration to be restated then). Needs lesson generation/renumbering by the pipeline, then a rebuild. PROPOSED ANSWER (for the teacher to approve or edit): No wording edit can settle this. The lesson plan now already has 16 lessons of 40 minutes each (15 teaching lessons plus Lesson 16 as the summative assessment), which matches the KICD allocation and the teacher decision. The proposed split of 8 double lessons is obsolete; approve it as resolved and restate totalDuration as 640 minutes in the unit overview. No lessons need to be added, split or trimmed. Alternative: Keep the 15+1 structure but make Lesson 16 a two-sitting assessment (Items 4 and 5(c) in a second sitting) without changing the lesson count. Also affects: Unit overview totalDuration must read 640 minutes (16 x 40); the Final Explanation is unchanged and its rubric should use the two KICD criteria and four levels already given, presented as a table.

records.value:
(a) Histogram: touching bars over 0 to <200 (height 5), 200 to <400 (9), 400 to <600 (0, so no bar), 600 to <800 (2), 800 to <1000 (1) and 1000 to <1200 (3), with axes labelled 'Gap length (m)' and 'Frequency' and a title. Polygon: midpoints 100, 300, 500, 700, 900, 1100 give the points (100, 5), (300, 9), (500, 0), (700, 2), (900, 1), (1100, 3), joined with straight lines and closed on the axis at (-100, 0) and (1300, 0). Description: the tallest bar is at 200 to <400 (9 gaps). There is a tall bar at 0 to <200 (5). The bar at 400 to <600 is empty (a gap in the graph). Then there are small bars at 600 to <800 (2) and 800 to <1000 (1), and a separate bar of 3 at 1000 to <1200. Most gaps are short, with a few long ones to the right.
(b) The merged class is three times wider than the others, so using frequency as height would make it look misleadingly tall. In a histogram, area shows frequency, so we use frequency density = frequency / class width. The merged class has 3 gaps (600, 700, 800) and width 600 m = 6 units of 100 m, so density = 3 / 6 = 0.5. It is the lowest bar even though it holds 3 gaps.
(c) The Mombasa Road polygon (frequencies 4, 8, 5, 2, 1, 0) is a single hump with a short tail and no gap of 1000 m or more. The Thika Road polygon (5, 9, 0, 2, 1, 3) has a second small rise at 1000 to <1200 m. So the means are similar (440 m and 380 m) but the shapes and spread differ. A mean alone cannot show this.

Polygon: midpoints 100, 300, 500, 700, 900, 1100 give the points (100, 5), (300, 9), (500, 0), (700, 2), (900, 1), (1100, 3), joined with straight lines and closed on the axis at (-100, 0) and (1300, 0). Description: the tallest bar is at 200 to <400 (9 gaps). There is a tall bar at 0 to <200 (5). The bar at 400 to <600 is empty (a gap in the graph). Then there are small bars at 600 to <800 (2) and 800 to <1000 (1), and a separate bar of 3 at 1000 to <1200. Most gaps are short, with a few long ones to the right.
(b) The merged class is three times wider than the others, so using frequency as height would make it look misleadingly tall. In a histogram, area shows frequency, so we use frequency density = frequency / class width. The merged class has 3 gaps (600, 700, 800) and width 600 m = 6 units of 100 m, so density = 3 / 6 = 0.5. It is the lowest bar even though it holds 3 gaps.
(c) The Mombasa Road polygon (frequencies 4, 8, 5, 2, 1, 0) is a single hump with a short tail and no gap of 1000 m or more. The Thika Road polygon (5, 9, 0, 2, 1, 3) has a second small rise at 1000 to <1200 m. So the means are similar (440 m and 380 m) but the shapes and spread differ. A mean alone cannot show this.
